sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
A bachelor's degree must appear on the transcript before graduate study begins; a master's is unnecessary.
UChicago bachelor's route is eligible in principle; admission depends on preparation and central academic
requirements. F-1 status is not a departmental exclusion. [s2] [s4]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Choose Mathematics PhD and fall term; identify pure/applied preference, up to three areas, and possible
supervisors. Those choices are nonbinding. Arrange three academic referees and verify any English exemption
before paying the application fee. [s3]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
No prior adviser agreement required in the public instructions. List possible faculty as nonbinding interests;
current appointment and supervision capacity must be checked. Sean Howe publicly welcomes meetings with
current Utah PhD students, which does not establish 2027 intake. [s3] [s11]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Department publishes section-by-section instructions and a link to the central application. Names, email
addresses and research selections route review; faculty interest is nonbinding. [s3]
Cycle verification [Standing rule]
Standing admissions rules updated February 2026; no explicit Fall 2027 deadline or stipend confirmation
found. Latest public bulletin read is 2025-26, revised May 2026. [s1] [s2] [s3] [s7]

sections.title: English and GRE
sections.text:
English requirement [Standing rule]
Central tests: TOEFL iBT 80 on the old scale or 4.5 on the new scale, IELTS 6.5, or DET 110; scores generally
within two years of application-fee payment. Teaching English assessment is separate; departmental materials
discuss stronger spoken/listening performance. [s5] [s1]
UChicago English exemption [Unresolved]
Central exemption covers a completed US bachelor's or higher degree within two years of paying the
application fee. Whether an unfinished UChicago degree qualifies at application is not established; obtain
confirmation before relying on exemption. Mathematics cannot independently waive the central rule. [s5] [s2]
GRE General [Standing rule]
Optional and considered if submitted; omission does not hurt. Unofficial scores accepted in application. [s2] [s3]
GRE Mathematics [Standing rule]
Optional and considered, especially relevant to pure mathematics; omission does not hurt. Unofficial scores
accepted; ETS institution 4853. [s2] [s3]

sections.title: Academic records

Transcripts and degree records [Standing rule]
Submit transcripts from every previously attended college or university. Degree must be posted before entry.
Central instructions govern acceptable international documents. [s3] [s4]
Mathematics-course list [Standing rule]
Helpful rather than explicitly mandatory: all mathematically related courses with short syllabus or textbook
descriptions; the application instructions link a sample. [s3]
Course descriptions [Standing rule]
Include short syllabus descriptions or textbooks in the helpful mathematics-course document. Follow the linked
example; a separate catalog-description upload is not established. [s3]

sections.title: Recommendation letters
sections.text:
Number and type [Standing rule]
Three letters; strongest sources are advanced mathematics instructors and research mentors. Referees may
explain unusual circumstances. [s3]
Scholarship references [Unresolved]
No extra initial scholarship reference requirement found in the departmental instructions. RTG eligibility is
separate; portal-specific additional questions remain unverified. [s3]
What sends the invitation [Standing rule]
Entering referee names and email addresses causes the application system to provide an upload link. Exact
send timing or an additional save/send action is not specified. [s3]

Before versus after submission [Unresolved]
Instructions associate invitations with entering referee details, but do not explicitly state whether submission is
required first. Confirm in the live portal without assuming. [s3]
Receipt confirmation [Unresolved]
Central admissions provides application-status access after submission. A letter-by-letter receipt indicator was
not independently established for Mathematics. [s4]
Updating and reusing letters [Unresolved]
Replacement, referee editing, letter updates and reuse in a later application are not explained in the public
Mathematics instructions. [s3]

sections.title: Written materials
sections.text:
Academic CV / resume [Standing rule]
CV/resume requested; any readable, organized format, no published length limit. Suggested content includes
awards, research/publications, thesis title and summary, conferences, teaching/mentoring, software and
languages; these experiences are not all expected. Portal file constraints unverified. [s3]
Statement of purpose [Standing rule]
Required upload. Faithful paraphrase: current mathematical interests, preparation/research, educational and
career aims, and why Utah fits; potential group/faculty, teaching, relevant difficulties and student activities
may help. No explicit word/page limit or typography rule. [s3] [s2]
Personal / background statement [Standing rule]
The department uses personal statement and statement of purpose for the same required document. A second
background essay is not listed; check the portal for additional central questions. [s3]
Research-interest statement [Standing rule]
Include research interests and possible groups/advisers in the SOP and select up to three areas in the
application. A separate research-interest essay is not listed; future choices are nonbinding. [s3]
Research proposal [Unresolved]
A formal research proposal is not listed in the public application instructions. Optional upload permission and
limits are unverified. [s3]
Writing sample / thesis / research summary [Unresolved]
No separate mandatory writing sample established. CV may give thesis/project title and brief summary;
permission to attach a full paper or thesis is unverified. [s3]
Publications list [Unresolved]
Publications may be listed in the CV. Separate list, full-paper upload or URL-link requirement not established.
[s3]
Course-list document [Standing rule]
Helpful mathematics-course document described above, using the linked example. No hard length/file limit
published. [s3]
Scholarship essays [Standing rule]
Ordinary PhD support is considered with admission. No separate initial essay established; RTG interest may be
mentioned in the SOP, but NSF RTG funds are restricted to US citizens/permanent residents. [s2] [s3]
Other short answers / materials [Unresolved]
Application includes central personal background, disciplinary and signature sections; exact live questions and
limits are not public. Do not infer an optional miscellaneous upload. [s3]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [Standing rule]
All admitted PhD applicants are offered a TA: approximately USD 27,000 per academic year plus tuition waiver
and health insurance, according to the undated FAQ. Summer support is decided annually and is not
guaranteed. Fall 2027 amount and residual fees require the offer. [s2]
Years of support [Prior cycle]
2025-26 bulletin revised May 2026 expects five years after a bachelor's, four after a master's. The actual
number of supported years is in the offer; extensions are discretionary, including reduced support in unusually
long cases. This is not a universal five-year guarantee. [s7]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
Ordinary PhD TA support is available within the all-admitted-students policy; NSF RTG funding expressly
excludes F-1-only applicants because it requires US citizenship/permanent residence. [s2] [s3]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Renewal depends on academic and teaching performance, exam/research milestones and at least 3.0 GPA for
tuition benefit. The bulletin permits continued enrollment without funding. Central tuition-benefit minima differ
from a Math offer; its projected 2027-28 minimum is not a departmental stipend promise. [s7] [s6]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
PhD admission application also handles financial aid. No separately required ordinary-TA application identified.
[s3] [s2]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
Summer teaching/research support may be offered annually. RA funding depends on funds and teaching
needs. RTG support is citizenship-restricted; external awards must be checked individually. [s2] [s3] [s7]
Application fee [Standing rule]
USD 65 international graduate application fee; USD 55 domestic. Central rules apply. [s4]
Fee waiver [Conflict]
Conflicting departmental text: limited waivers sometimes include students already in the US on F-1/J-1, yet the
next sentence excludes international students. Ask Paula Tooman (tooman@math.utah.edu), subject
Application Fee Waiver, before using a code; unauthorized codes cause rejection. Central McNair
documentation route also exists. [s3] [s4]

sections.title: Potential advisers and recent research
sections.text:
Algebraic / arithmetic geometry
Christopher Hacon
Birational geometry, minimal models, singularities, and analytic/Kähler extensions of algebraic-geometric
methods. [s8] [s9]
Current faculty affiliation verified; 2027 supervision availability not stated.
Research evidence: 2024 · ACC for generalized log canonical thresholds for complex analytic spaces
Topic evidence from the official faculty publication page.
Tommaso de Fernex
Birational geometry and singularities; arc spaces and motivic integration. [s8] [s10]
Current faculty affiliation verified; 2027 supervision availability not stated.
Research evidence: 2026 · On arc fibers of morphisms of schemes
Topic evidence from the official faculty publication page.
Karl Schwede
Positive- and mixed-characteristic singularities, commutative algebra, perfectoid methods and thresholds. [s8]
[s12]
Current faculty affiliation verified; 2027 supervision availability not stated.
Research evidence: 2026 · The Briançon-Skoda theorem for pseudo-rational and Du Bois singularities and uniformity in
excellent rings
Topic evidence from the official faculty publication page.
Sean Howe
Arithmetic geometry, p-adic Hodge theory, period spaces and representation-theoretic interactions. [s8] [s11]
Associate professor from July 2026; 2027 supervision capacity unknown.
Research evidence: 2026 · Admissible pairs and p-adic Hodge structures II: The bi-analytic Ax-Lindemann theorem
Topic evidence from the official faculty publication page.
Aaron Bertram
Algebraic geometry; the official CV includes tropical algebraic geometry, but the available CV is historical and
does not establish recent research. [s8] [s14]
Current faculty affiliation verified; 2027 supervision availability not stated.
Research evidence: 2017; historical · Tropical Nullstellensatz for congruences
Topic evidence from the official faculty publication page.
Representation theory
David Schwein
p-adic representation theory, supercuspidal representations, local Langlands packets and ramification. [s8] [s13]
Assistant professor since 2025; 2027 supervision capacity unknown.
Research evidence: 2025 preprint · Construction of tame supercuspidal representations in arbitrary residue characteristic
Topic evidence from the official faculty publication page.

Representation theory / number theory
Gordan Savin
Representations of reductive groups over local fields, exceptional theta correspondences, local Langlands and
automorphic forms. [s8] [s16] [gapc20] [gapc21]
Professor in Utah's current official directory.
Research evidence: 2025 · The dual pair Aut(C) × F4 (p-adic case)
Edmund Karasiewicz and Gordan Savin; published October 16, 2025, Forum of Mathematics, Sigma 13, e174. Studies exceptional
local theta correspondence using minimal representations, Jacquet modules and Fourier-Jacobi functors.

Algebraic geometry
Yuan-Pin Lee
Gromov-Witten theory, quantum K-theory, moduli of curves, birational and enumerative geometry; recent work
on logarithmic double ramification classes. [s15] [gapc22] [gapc23] [gapc24] [gapc25]

Submitted July 15, 2026; six authors including Lee. Constructs a K-theoretic class with product and GLr(Z)-invariance formulas;
primary arXiv record and author's official-profile-linked research page agree.

Pay attention to
• Do not use a fee-waiver code until the contradictory F-1 policy is resolved.
• A still-in-progress UChicago degree may not satisfy the English exemption at application.
• Use January 1 for planning; late-deadline sources conflict.
• Older research rosters list faculty who have moved or changed appointment.
• Faculty coverage is a partial shortlist, not an exhaustive adviser census.
• Adjunct status and primary Sinica appointment mean Utah doctoral-supervision availability must be
confirmed; do not describe him as a full-time resident Utah professor.
Eligibility and preparation
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
A bachelor's degree must appear on the transcript before graduate study begins; a master's is unnecessary.
UChicago bachelor's route is eligible in principle; admission depends on preparation and central academic
requirements. F-1 status is not a departmental exclusion. [s2] [s4]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Choose Mathematics PhD and fall term; identify pure/applied preference, up to three areas, and possible
supervisors. Those choices are nonbinding. Arrange three academic referees and verify any English exemption
before paying the application fee. [s3]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
No prior adviser agreement required in the public instructions. List possible faculty as nonbinding interests;
current appointment and supervision capacity must be checked. Sean Howe publicly welcomes meetings with
current Utah PhD students, which does not establish 2027 intake. [s3] [s11]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Department publishes section-by-section instructions and a link to the central application. Names, email
addresses and research selections route review; faculty interest is nonbinding. [s3]
Cycle verification [Standing rule]
Standing admissions rules updated February 2026; no explicit Fall 2027 deadline or stipend confirmation
found. Latest public bulletin read is 2025-26, revised May 2026. [s1] [s2] [s3] [s7]
Deadlines by stage
Academic application [Conflict]
January 1 annually for full consideration; 2027 year and time zone not explicitly stated. Late applications: FAQ
says March 15, program page April 1, only if places remain. [s1] [s2]
Funding consideration [Standing rule]
January 1 annually for full admission and financial-aid consideration; 2027 and time zone unconfirmed. [s2]

January 1 full-consideration target; no distinct public grace period or clock time established. Confirm whether

Accepting an offer [Standing rule]
Program page gives April 15 as the decision deadline. This is standing departmental language, not
independently confirmed Fall 2027 CGS participation; follow the actual offer and any check-ins. [s1]
English and GRE
English requirement [Standing rule]
Central tests: TOEFL iBT 80 on the old scale or 4.5 on the new scale, IELTS 6.5, or DET 110; scores generally
within two years of application-fee payment. Teaching English assessment is separate; departmental materials
discuss stronger spoken/listening performance. [s5] [s1]
UChicago English exemption [Unresolved]
Central exemption covers a completed US bachelor's or higher degree within two years of paying the
application fee. Whether an unfinished UChicago degree qualifies at application is not established; obtain
confirmation before relying on exemption. Mathematics cannot independently waive the central rule. [s5] [s2]
GRE General [Standing rule]
Optional and considered if submitted; omission does not hurt. Unofficial scores accepted in application. [s2] [s3]
GRE Mathematics [Standing rule]
Optional and considered, especially relevant to pure mathematics; omission does not hurt. Unofficial scores
accepted; ETS institution 4853. [s2] [s3]
Academic records
Transcripts and degree records [Standing rule]
Submit transcripts from every previously attended college or university. Degree must be posted before entry.
Central instructions govern acceptable international documents. [s3] [s4]
Mathematics-course list [Standing rule]
Helpful rather than explicitly mandatory: all mathematically related courses with short syllabus or textbook
descriptions; the application instructions link a sample. [s3]
Course descriptions [Standing rule]
Include short syllabus descriptions or textbooks in the helpful mathematics-course document. Follow the linked
example; a separate catalog-description upload is not established. [s3]
Recommendation letters
Number and type [Standing rule]
Three letters; strongest sources are advanced mathematics instructors and research mentors. Referees may
explain unusual circumstances. [s3]
Scholarship references [Unresolved]
No extra initial scholarship reference requirement found in the departmental instructions. RTG eligibility is
separate; portal-specific additional questions remain unverified. [s3]
What sends the invitation [Standing rule]
Entering referee names and email addresses causes the application system to provide an upload link. Exact
send timing or an additional save/send action is not specified. [s3]

Instructions associate invitations with entering referee details, but do not explicitly state whether submission is
required first. Confirm in the live portal without assuming. [s3]
Receipt confirmation [Unresolved]
Central admissions provides application-status access after submission. A letter-by-letter receipt indicator was
not independently established for Mathematics. [s4]
Updating and reusing letters [Unresolved]
Replacement, referee editing, letter updates and reuse in a later application are not explained in the public
Mathematics instructions. [s3]
Written materials
Academic CV / resume [Standing rule]
CV/resume requested; any readable, organized format, no published length limit. Suggested content includes
awards, research/publications, thesis title and summary, conferences, teaching/mentoring, software and
languages; these experiences are not all expected. Portal file constraints unverified. [s3]
Statement of purpose [Standing rule]
Required upload. Faithful paraphrase: current mathematical interests, preparation/research, educational and
career aims, and why Utah fits; potential group/faculty, teaching, relevant difficulties and student activities
may help. No explicit word/page limit or typography rule. [s3] [s2]
Personal / background statement [Standing rule]
The department uses personal statement and statement of purpose for the same required document. A second
background essay is not listed; check the portal for additional central questions. [s3]
Research-interest statement [Standing rule]
Include research interests and possible groups/advisers in the SOP and select up to three areas in the
application. A separate research-interest essay is not listed; future choices are nonbinding. [s3]
Research proposal [Unresolved]
A formal research proposal is not listed in the public application instructions. Optional upload permission and
limits are unverified. [s3]
Writing sample / thesis / research summary [Unresolved]
No separate mandatory writing sample established. CV may give thesis/project title and brief summary;
permission to attach a full paper or thesis is unverified. [s3]
Publications list [Unresolved]
Publications may be listed in the CV. Separate list, full-paper upload or URL-link requirement not established.
[s3]
Course-list document [Standing rule]
Helpful mathematics-course document described above, using the linked example. No hard length/file limit
published. [s3]
Scholarship essays [Standing rule]
Ordinary PhD support is considered with admission. No separate initial essay established; RTG interest may be
mentioned in the SOP, but NSF RTG funds are restricted to US citizens/permanent residents. [s2] [s3]
Other short answers / materials [Unresolved]
Application includes central personal background, disciplinary and signature sections; exact live questions and
limits are not public. Do not infer an optional miscellaneous upload. [s3]

Funding and fees
Amount and coverage [Standing rule]
All admitted PhD applicants are offered a TA: approximately USD 27,000 per academic year plus tuition waiver
and health insurance, according to the undated FAQ. Summer support is decided annually and is not
guaranteed. Fall 2027 amount and residual fees require the offer. [s2]
Years of support [Prior cycle]
2025-26 bulletin revised May 2026 expects five years after a bachelor's, four after a master's. The actual
number of supported years is in the offer; extensions are discretionary, including reduced support in unusually
long cases. This is not a universal five-year guarantee. [s7]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
Ordinary PhD TA support is available within the all-admitted-students policy; NSF RTG funding expressly
excludes F-1-only applicants because it requires US citizenship/permanent residence. [s2] [s3]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Renewal depends on academic and teaching performance, exam/research milestones and at least 3.0 GPA for
tuition benefit. The bulletin permits continued enrollment without funding. Central tuition-benefit minima differ
from a Math offer; its projected 2027-28 minimum is not a departmental stipend promise. [s7] [s6]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
PhD admission application also handles financial aid. No separately required ordinary-TA application identified.
[s3] [s2]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
Summer teaching/research support may be offered annually. RA funding depends on funds and teaching
needs. RTG support is citizenship-restricted; external awards must be checked individually. [s2] [s3] [s7]
Application fee [Standing rule]
USD 65 international graduate application fee; USD 55 domestic. Central rules apply. [s4]
Fee waiver [Conflict]
Conflicting departmental text: limited waivers sometimes include students already in the US on F-1/J-1, yet the
next sentence excludes international students. Ask Paula Tooman (tooman@math.utah.edu), subject
Application Fee Waiver, before using a code; unauthorized codes cause rejection. Central McNair
documentation route also exists. [s3] [s4]
Conflicts and remaining checks
Conflicting sources [Conflict]
Late deadline differs (March 15 FAQ versus April 1 program page). F-1/J-1 waiver exception conflicts with
blanket international exclusion in the same text. Older research listings can be stale: Harold Blum is now
Georgia Tech; Yuan-Pin Lee's current university appointment is adjunct. [s1] [s2] [s3] [s8] [s15]
Checks still needed [Unresolved]
Confirm 2027 deadlines/time zone, pending-US-degree English exemption, F-1 fee-waiver eligibility, letter
receipt/update mechanics, full support duration/residual fees and summer terms. Faculty shortlist below is
incomplete: additional algebra/representation faculty need current-paper checks; adviser availability is not
established. [s1] [s2] [s3] [s4] [s5] [s8]

CV/resume requested; any readable, organized format, no published length limit. Suggested content includes
awards, research/publications, thesis title and summary, conferences, teaching/mentoring, software and
languages; these experiences are not all expected. Portal file constraints unverified. [s3]
Statement of purpose [Standing rule]
Required upload. Faithful paraphrase: current mathematical interests, preparation/research, educational and
career aims, and why Utah fits; potential group/faculty, teaching, relevant difficulties and student activities
may help. No explicit word/page limit or typography rule. [s3] [s2]

background essay is not listed; check the portal for additional central questions. [s3]

Funding and fees
Amount and coverage [Standing rule]
All admitted PhD applicants are offered a TA: approximately USD 27,000 per academic year plus tuition waiver
and health insurance, according to the undated FAQ. Summer support is decided annually and is not
guaranteed. Fall 2027 amount and residual fees require the offer. [s2]
Years of support [Prior cycle]
2025-26 bulletin revised May 2026 expects five years after a bachelor's, four after a master's. The actual
number of supported years is in the offer; extensions are discretionary, including reduced support in unusually
long cases. This is not a universal five-year guarantee. [s7]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
Ordinary PhD TA support is available within the all-admitted-students policy; NSF RTG funding expressly
excludes F-1-only applicants because it requires US citizenship/permanent residence. [s2] [s3]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Renewal depends on academic and teaching performance, exam/research milestones and at least 3.0 GPA for
tuition benefit. The bulletin permits continued enrollment without funding. Central tuition-benefit minima differ
from a Math offer; its projected 2027-28 minimum is not a departmental stipend promise. [s7] [s6]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
PhD admission application also handles financial aid. No separately required ordinary-TA application identified.
[s3] [s2]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
Summer teaching/research support may be offered annually. RA funding depends on funds and teaching
needs. RTG support is citizenship-restricted; external awards must be checked individually. [s2] [s3] [s7]
Application fee [Standing rule]
USD 65 international graduate application fee; USD 55 domestic. Central rules apply. [s4]
Fee waiver [Conflict]
Conflicting departmental text: limited waivers sometimes include students already in the US on F-1/J-1, yet the
next sentence excludes international students. Ask Paula Tooman (tooman@math.utah.edu), subject
Application Fee Waiver, before using a code; unauthorized codes cause rejection. Central McNair
documentation route also exists. [s3] [s4]
